readout_other: Ex-vivo fluorescence imaging (Azure Sapphire) of IRDye800-1kDa tracer distribution in brain sections to quantify glymphatic influx; physiological monitoring (heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen level, perfusion, body/pad temperature) via PhysioSuite
direction_notes: FUS significantly enhanced glymphatic tracer transport across all isoflurane anesthesia levels (main effect of FUS, p=7.70x10^-7); anesthesia depth independently affected transport (p=7.45x10^-11) but did not interact significantly with FUS treatment (p=0.106), indicating the FUS effect was independent of anesthetic depth. This is a fluid-transport outcome, not a measure of neuronal excitation/inhibition.
safety_notes: No statistically significant differences in pad/rectal temperature, oxygen level, heart rate, or perfusion were observed during sonication across anesthesia sub-groups in Ultrasound vs Control groups; a decrease in respiratory rate was observed under FUS at heavy (3%) anesthesia, though this could not be solely attributed to ultrasound.

exposures.label: Brain-wide grid-pattern FUS for glymphatic transport enhancement

timing.protocol_description: A 650 kHz spherically focused transducer was swept across the entire rat brain in a grid pattern (six 3 mm x 14 mm sub-loops, START (0,0) to STOP (18,14)), with each loop taking ~27.12 s plus a 50 ms pause, for a total of 30 loops per rat. Sham procedures used the identical trajectory with zero input power. Rats were under 1.5%, 2%, or 3% isoflurane anesthesia during sonication, beginning 10 min after intrathecal tracer injection.

exposures.label: In-vivo calibration: focal vascular barrier opening validation

target.label: focal targeted brain region used to validate transducer targeting/coupling (region not further specified)

timing.protocol_description: To confirm the ultrasound field's in-vivo targeting/coupling, a vascular barrier opening assay was performed with an established ultrasound pulse (650 kHz, 1 PRF, 1 min, 0.35 MPa) combined with an ultrasound contrast agent (Optison), in 5 rats designated for calibration.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Healthy male Sprague Dawley rats were obtained from Charles River and used after acclimation for 3 d. A total of 35 rats were used in this study. Among them, <sup>fi</sup>ve rats were speci<sup>fi</sup>cally designated for in-vivo calibration involving vascular barrier opening, while the remaining 30 rats were utilized for ultrasonic glymphatic manipulation.
source_quotes.sham_type: For sham procedures, the identical positioning and trajectory were employed, but the input power to the ultrasound transducer was zero.
source_quotes.adverse_events: Among these parameters, such as pad temperature regulating body heat within the 36 −37°C range, rectal temperature, oxygen levels, heart rate, and perfusion, no statistically signi<sup>fi</sup>cant differences were observed during sonication across various anesthetic sub-groups in both Ultrasound and Control groups, as depicted in Figure 3A.

flags.reason: Abstract/results state the ultrasound exposure lasted 10 min, but the methods describe the grid-sweep trajectory (30 loops) taking approximately 14 min to complete; both durations are recorded as a list due to this text-text discrepancy.
The 0.2 MPa in-situ pressure is based on an assumed 30% pressure insertion loss for skull attenuation rather than a direct measurement through skull in this cohort; classified as derating.

Represents the four groups (3 anesthesia-level glymphatic FUS+ groups of n=5 each, plus n=5 calibration animals) that received active ultrasound; paper gives only group sizes (Table 1), not an overall total exposed to ultrasound.
Text states '1PRF' for the calibration pulse; interpreted as PRF = 1 Hz, but this notation is ambiguous.
The specific brain region targeted for the vascular-barrier-opening calibration assay is not explicitly named in the text (only 'targeted brain regions').
